command_activity.command:
/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    t=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (p/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
    texts.append(f'\\n\\n=== PAGE {i} ===\\n{t}')
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency bottleneck with a simple approach: reuse CLIP attention and key features to prune and merge visual tokens before the expensive language model. The compression module introduces no additional learned parameters.

PruMerge+ demonstrates a useful accuracy–token tradeoff across six image benchmarks and two model sizes. With 25% of tokens, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2, 57.1 versus 58.2 on TextVQA, and 64.9 versus 64.3 on MMBench (Table 1).

Training-free transfer to Video-LLaVA provides evidence of broader applicability. Table 3 reports substantial token reduction while preserving most benchmark performance and improving ActivityNet-QA accuracy from 45.3 to 48.3 with PruMerge.

Sampling, component, and fine-tuning ablations provide useful supporting evidence. The pipeline diagrams aid understanding, and the manuscript cites the underlying models, datasets, and relevant token-reduction methods.
weaknesses: The comparative experiments do not establish matched training conditions. PruMerge+ in Table 7 uses the fine-tuned results from Table 1, but equivalent fine-tuning for ToMe, ATS, and EViT is not documented; CrossGet results are imported from its paper. Consequently, the reported superiority cannot be cleanly attributed to the proposed compression method.

Practical acceleration remains insufficiently validated. Table 2 explicitly reports roofline estimates rather than measured runtime, without end-to-end measurements covering compression overhead, decoding, or variable-length batching. Furthermore, the claimed O(n) clustering complexity conflicts with the described pairwise similarity computation: comparing m anchors against n tokens costs O(mnd), which is quadratic in n when the retention fraction is fixed.

Important implementation details are unresolved. Algorithm 1 adds m spatial tokens to m anchors, which does not explain the reported increase from 5.5% retention for PruMerge to 25% for PruMerge+; its subsequent loop and output still reference only m tokens. The neighborhood size k and LoRA configuration are unspecified, and the merge equation omits both weight normalization and the anchor despite the prose describing weighted averaging and supplementation. These ambiguities hinder reproduction of the strongest results.

The claims of maintaining performance at aggressive compression are overstated. For the 7B model, PruMerge reduces VQAv2 from 78.5 to 72.0, POPE from 85.9 to 76.3, and MME from 1510.7 to 1350.3 (Table 1). Section 4.1 also claims improved POPE performance, although every proposed variant scores below its corresponding baseline. The promising fourfold-reduction results should be distinguished from these larger losses.

The distinctive contribution of adaptive IQR selection is not isolated. The sampling baselines use sequential or uniform selection, without comparing against fixed-budget CLS-attention top-k selection followed by the same merging procedure. Threshold sensitivity and quantitative evidence connecting outlier counts to image complexity are also absent. Thus, the benefit of the central adaptive mechanism over simpler attention-based selection remains uncertain.
